name: First Yang Cancellation Page Is Cut-Nerve Homology
statement: Fix a partition $\pi$ of an ample family $H$ into $k$ parts. Let $\mathcal A_\pi$ be the latent charts whose failure arcs stay within parts, and let $\mathcal N_\pi$ consist of chart sets that fail to make some part strongly connected. The row $q=k-2$ of the first differential of the Yang failure-cover spectral sequence is the direct sum, over all $k$-part partitions, of the relative chain complexes $C_\bullet(2^{\mathcal A_\pi},\mathcal N_\pi;\mathbb F_2)$. Hence $E^2_{p,k-2}\cong\bigoplus_{|\pi|=k}\widetilde H_{p-1}(\mathcal N_\pi;\mathbb F_2)$. Moreover $\mathcal N_\pi$ is homotopy equivalent to the nerve $\mathcal K_\pi$ of the canonical cover indexed by directed cuts within parts, where a cut simplex consists of charts having no arc leaving that cut. Consequently, if $H$ is nonpeelable, then for some $k$-part partition $\pi$, $\widetilde H_{|H|-k-1}(\mathcal K_\pi;\mathbb F_2)\ne0$.
proof: A first-page sphere summand belongs to partition $\pi$ exactly when all arcs stay within parts and strongly connect every part; these are precisely the faces of the simplex $2^{\mathcal A_\pi}$ outside $\mathcal N_\pi$. Removing a chart induces the identity in the same row when all parts remain strongly connected and zero there when a part splits, giving the relative simplicial boundary and the second-page formula. A directed graph is strongly connected exactly when every nontrivial cut has an outgoing arc, so $\mathcal N_\pi$ is the union of the displayed cut simplices. Their intersections are simplices, and the nerve lemma gives $\mathcal N_\pi\simeq\mathcal K_\pi$. A surviving class of total degree $|H|-2$ then yields the final necessary homology class.
